prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation. Automation: bay monitoring/control, station coordination, external interfaces. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): sequencing, interlocks, timestamps changes; produces Bay Status Digest (Glasswing uses for current conditions); preserves separate bay scopes; requests Breaker Control Unit ops only if mode/permissives allow. North Bay Controller, South Bay Controller: own-bay control/interlocking per approved sequence; separate scopes, no substitution; North blocks close if interlocks not ready; bay boundary sets device authority and confirming indications; shared equipment needs explicit coordination. Breaker Control Unit: executes permitted commands only when conditions met; local interlocks. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): independent protection; approved setting group; produces Relay Diagnostic Note (to Larkspur). North Protection Panel; Transformer Protection Panel (authority independent of switching). Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): current indications, no protection; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip. Station Gateway: external boundary; produces Protocol Retry Summary. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): time reference; produces Clock Drift Snapshot (to Orchard); synchronized/degraded/unavailable; loss never discards evidence. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): authoritative evidence as received (source, event/receipt time, quality); flags uncertain/corrected times; config/access history; role-limited, audited; retention, investigation holds, health/recovery checks, backup. Maintenance Remote Terminal (no authority). Station DC System: produces Battery Load Test Record. Engineering Workstation: revision-controlled config; produces Settings Review Receipt; bounded queries; exports keep flags; interpretation separate from evidence. Actors: Control Room Operator: directs, may suspend; sends switching requests to Keystone; reviews alarms (priority, source, time, bay indications), new vs standing; protection operation/unexplained state requires prompt investigation; authorizes return to automation. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): station-wide plan; checks clearances; produces Isolation Boundary Card; confirms handback (evidence stays for engineering review). Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): settings, disturbance and coordination review; independent reviewer. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): verifies device identity/conditions; sends Breaker Inspection Tag. Substation Supervisor: authorization, priority conflicts, exceptional switching authority. Requirements: local before remote; interlocks authoritative; sequences define order, hold points, stop conditions; settings: unique revision, independent review, checks, outage window, post-install compare.

New part:
S151: The Control Room Operator acknowledges alarms only after reviewing the indication and retains awareness of any condition that remains unresolved.
S152: The Control Room Operator uses the acknowledgement slip to record the alarm response and any outstanding action.
S153: The operator checks available device status and sequence information without treating a cleared indication as proof that the underlying cause has been corrected.
S154: The Feeder Protection Relay indication is reviewed against the affected feeder status and any related protection operation.
S155: The Bay Automation Controller provides bay-level status indications that support the operator’s assessment of the alarm.
S156: Glasswing shall retain alarm state and event information for operator review after an indication has cleared.
S157: The Sequence Event Archive provides time-ordered evidence for later operational review.
S158: The North Protection Panel contains the protection equipment associated with feeder protection functions.
S159: The Control Room Operator uses indications from the North Protection Panel to assess feeder protection operations and related alarms.
S160: The Transformer Protection Panel is dedicated to protection functions associated with the power transformer rather than feeder protection.
S161: The Transformer Protection Panel provides local indication of transformer protection operation for assessment during an alarm response.
S162: The Control Room Operator considers the condition of the Station DC System when alarms or protection indications suggest a possible control-power concern.
S163: A breaker status discrepancy is treated as an abnormal condition until its cause and operational significance are understood.
S164: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized review of protection and event information, not as a substitute for immediate operational assessment.
S165: The Protection Relay Engineer supports investigation when relay indications, settings concerns, or event evidence require technical interpretation.
S166: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S167: The Substation Supervisor is consulted when the alarm response requires escalation beyond routine operator actions.
S168: The Control Room Operator produces the Clearance Handoff Memo when an unresolved alarm condition requires a formal handoff.
S169: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback before the associated state-change evidence is considered available for authorized engineering review.
S170: After handback, the Control Room Operator verifies that alarm status, equipment status, and recorded evidence are consistent before closing the response.
S171: The station communications design separates supervisory requests, bay-level execution, and protection action so loss of one layer does not silently substitute for another.
S172: Station Gateway brokers authorized station traffic across control-room and bay networks, applying configured protocol mappings, addressing, and access controls.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
